What degraded

  • Re-verification: about 57 docket items remain past their leash, behind crawl boundaries or 403s. Nothing was routed around.
  • The 30 deterministic movement lines reverify.py wrote were not reworded.
  • Scanner: no Cloudflare D1 or Worker access in this session, so today's scan count and the live DAILY_CAP are UNKNOWN.
  • Grid watch: November 1st is missing from the series and ERCOT can't backfill it (gridwatch_pagecheck exit 2, advisory).
  • BESPOKE departure: after critic round 2 the under-8 frames got repair rounds instead of rebuilds from second concepts.
  • The deck shipped at 7.33 against an 8.0 bar, at the round cap after four rounds. Art median 7.5.
  • Instagram and Facebook Stories are BLOCKED: no reviewed 9:16 adaptation of the frames was made this run.
  • Effort read medium at wake although .claude/settings.json asks for high.

Named here rather than left out. A run that quietly ships less than it planned teaches nobody anything.

1. The post copy

Texas A&M says Florida's state drone team made its tool standard procedure.

CLARKE rates the damage to each building in a color coded view. A road model flags damaged roads so crews can route around them. A trained operator reviews every assessment before it reaches decision makers.

Tom Manzini of the development team says CLARKE turns drone imagery into damage assessments in minutes instead of 18 to 24 hours.

Texas A&M says the models learned from more than 21,000 damaged homes in 10 major disasters, Hurricane Harvey among them. It says 125 responders from 63 agencies in 14 states and Puerto Rico have trained on CLARKE. The November 24th release and the project site name no Texas agency or county among its users.

How many of those 63 agencies are in Texas?

#TexasAM #CLARKE #HurricaneHarvey

The machine changed itself

  • The kit person can press a modelled index finger onto a point (handShape press).
    Frame 6's operator was built by hand with a capsule finger and read as a mannequin to every judge.
  • layout_check now blocks bleeds, GRID pieces and accent findings on a bespoke run during the run. Only the rotation stays report-only.
    Nos. 82, 83 and 86 each reconciled dossiers at ship after shipped_check refused what layout_check had passed.
  • fig_inject no longer treats a FIG named inside a string literal as a dynamic read.
    Nos. 80 and 86 had every figure injected into frames whose own guards then threw.
  • caption_check refuses a clause printed twice in a row, and copy_sync_check refuses a copy.json caption that differs from caption.txt.
    This run's round 3 hard fail was a doubled caption opener that both gates passed.
  • plan_render_check reads past the render report's 320 character text window.
    Frame 9's long dek was reported missing although the frame carried it, and the run cut its action line to pass.

Every change is logged in ledger/carousel/upgrades.json.

Notes

The record came first. Two items were admitted. tx-2026-0258 is Texas A&M's CLARKE, built at College Station and filed under Brazos County by the November 22nd rule. tx-2026-0259 is Texas Tech's Critical Infrastructure Telecom Ecosystem Incubator at Reese, in Lubbock County. Three items moved and were brought current with dated movement lines. PUCT Project 58000 now counts 72 filings, after Oncor's November 19th rate impact analysis and a November 24th staff redline memo. The Kerrville screwworm item now counts 95 premises, and Cameron County joined the zone. The Wiwynn El Paso date was re-quoted. Forty two items were re-verified and stamped. About 57 remain past their leash behind crawl boundaries or 403s, and that shortfall is named rather than capped. Held as leads. ERCOT's Batch Zero verification update (the PDF answered 403), Tarrant County's abatement guidelines vote and Cameron County's SpaceX abatement vote (journalism only), the FAA SMART tool at DFW, Presidio's Mainspring units, Mesquite ISD's AI drafting, MD Anderson's digital twin projects, Firefly in Cedar Park and Modine in Grand Prairie. The deck. Carousel no. 86 tells CLARKE in nine bespoke frames, from a damaged subdivision read roof by roof to frame 1's camera over undamaged Texas ground, where the gold route stops short of every lot. It shipped at 7.33 after four panel rounds. Round 3 hard failed a doubled caption opener that this run's own repair script wrote. It was repaired, copy.json was regenerated from caption.txt, and round 4 cleared it. All three judges still charge frame 7's root plate, frame 4's rims, frame 6's mannequin operator and a close that repeats the cover. They also charge a deck that saves the Florida news for frame 9, and the third drone deck in five days. At ship, shipped_check refused five things the run's own gates had passed. The gold accent measured on no frame because its glow turned it lemon. The FIG lines were stale. Two dossier bleeds and one GRID declaration were wrong. The ledger prose carried a number word. Each was fixed rather than waived, and frames 1 and 9 went back to the art director. The weekly machine pass came due and made five changes. The caption checks that missed the hard fail now refuse it. Prompt audit, the final reading. 2,331 tool calls were measured, and 68 showed a permission decision wait. Every one was an Agent, SendMessage or short Bash call, and the longest was 30.1 seconds. That timing matches the permission classifier deciding rather than a dialog a person answered, and nothing in the run stalled. No-stall hook. Armed at 05:03:18 UTC. At session start it judged the session unattended, and the host's CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ATTENDED was 0. It refused nothing. Social delivery runs after the merge through Upload-Post REST, and its receipts are added to this draft.

This email is a draft. Nothing was sent by email. The deck is already merged to main, so these links are live. Social publishing is handled by the automation; destination receipts report what actually published.
